papers.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
papers.authors: Anish Ghoshal, Alessandro Strumia
papers.abstract: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $φ$ couples via the effective operator $φ\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. Embedding $φ$ as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory requires an anomaly coefficient $\gtrsim100$, implying a Landau pole for QCD. These tensions are relaxed for more strongly coupled dark gauge sectors.

papers.title: VLT and Keck recovery and characterisation of 2025 SC$_{79}$: linking 'Ayló'chaxnim and Atira asteroids
papers.authors: Bryce T. Bolin, Leo Y. Alcorn, Davide Farnocchia, Marco Delbo, Martina Baratella, Henri M. J. Boffin, Max Brodheim, Alexa Gordon, Lordrick Kahinga, Michael Lundquist, Rita Morris, J. Xavier Prochaska
papers.abstract: Asteroids near the boundary between the Atira and 'Ayló'chaxnim classes can trace dynamical links between the two populations, but their small solar elongations make recovery and physical characterisation difficult. We recover 2025 SC$_{79}$, measure its optical colours, and investigate its likely source region and transitions between these populations. We combine Keck/LRIS astrometry and VLT/FORS2 four-filter photometry with Bus-DeMeo taxonomic comparisons, published source-model probabilities, and integrations of 10,000 clones drawn from the covariance of JPL solution #2 and followed for 5 Myr in each direction. The SDSS-equivalent colours are $g-r=0.8254_{-0.1339}^{+0.2136}$, $r-i=0.1764_{-0.0540}^{+0.0523}$ and $i-z=-0.4975_{-0.1162}^{+0.1055}$ mag. The V-type class mean gives the closest colour match. At the V-type median albedo $p_V=0.362$, $H=18.83\pm0.15$ mag implies a diameter of $0.379^{+0.027}_{-0.025}$ km. The source model assigns a combined probability of 95.4% to delivery channels associated with the inner Main Belt. The ensemble-mean 'Ayló'chaxnim/Atira residence fractions are 30.2%/69.8% over the preceding 100 kyr and 3.6%/96.0% over the following 100 kyr; the remaining 0.4% of future ensemble time follows collision removal. Clones spend an average of 231 kyr in the 'Ayló'chaxnim class over the preceding 500 kyr and 120 kyr over the following 500 kyr. In the 5-Myr forward integrations, 14.56% of clones collide with Venus, 3.77% with Mercury and 0.22% with Earth. The V-like colours and source-model probabilities favour an origin in the inner Main Belt for 2025 SC$_{79}$. Its clones move between the 'Ayló'chaxnim and Atira populations.

papers.title: SN 2026ahvu in NGC 1433 May Be a Prompt Type Ia Supernova with a Delay Time Under 100 Myr
papers.authors: Sumit K. Sarbadhicary, Kiana Henny, Adam Leroy, Karin Sandstrom, Kirsten L. Larson, David A. Thilker, Gagandeep S. Anand, Ashley T. Barnes, Laura A. Lopez, Daniel Maschmann, Marco Troncoso, Hwihyun Kim, Janice C. Lee, Frank Bigiel, Médéric Boquien, Rupali Chandar, Ryan Chown, Daniel A. Dale, Sinan Deger, Oleg V. Egorov, Simon C. O. Glover, Oleg Y. Gnedin, Jay González Lobos, Hao He, Rebecca J. Houghton, Debosmita Pathak, M. Jimena Rodriguez, Eva Schinnerer, Michael Tucker, Tony D. Weinbeck, Thomas G. Williams, Bradley C. Whitmore, Leonardo Ubeda
papers.abstract: SN 2026ahvu is a Type Ia supernova (SN) that occurred in the nearby galaxy NGC 1433. Using archival Hubble and JWST imaging from the PHANGS survey, we show that the SN lies within 0.19$''$ and 0.26$''$ of two UV-bright star clusters. This $0.19/0.26''$ separation corresponds to $8/11$ pc ($17/24$ pc) at the reported distances of $9.1$ and $18.9$ Mpc, respectively. The probability of finding an unrelated Type Ia SN this close to a cataloged star cluster by chance is only $\sim$0.4 %. Thus, SN 2026ahvu is likely the first Type Ia SN that can be associated with relatively young star clusters in a nearby galaxy. From spectral energy distribution fitting using HST+JWST (or HST-only) data, we find that the clusters have age estimates of $37_{-5}^{+3}$ ($57_{-9}^{+14}$) Myr and $95_{-13}^{+15}$ ($88_{-12}^{+14}$) Myr. Association with either cluster would mean that SN 2026ahvu should be considered a prompt SN Ia and provide one of the most concrete measurements to date of a prompt Ia delay time. The median age of the younger star cluster is close to the minimum possible delay time for SN Ia progenitors. If the SN is indeed associated with the younger cluster, it would imply that Type Ia SNe can occur almost immediately after white dwarf formation. If the SN is associated with the older cluster, this discovery still presents the first example of a prompt Type Ia SN with delay time under 100 Myr.

papers.title: Multi-phase Carbon Structure and Dynamics in NGC 6334: Insights from CO, [C I], and [C II]
papers.authors: S. Neupane, F. Wyrowski, N. Schneider, A. G. G. M. Tielens, R. Simon, J. S. Urquhart, R. Güsten, M-Y. Lee, D. Russeil, G. Garay, R. Higgins, K. M. Menten
papers.abstract: We present high-angular and velocity resolution observations of the emission lines of [CII] at 158 micron, [CI] at 609 micron, and the 12CO and 13CO (J=3-2) transitions toward the central region of NGC 6334, providing a detailed multi-phase view of carbon in this massive star-forming complex. By combining morphology and spatial scales information, kinematics, line profiles, and line ratio analyses, we quantify the distribution and physical state of ionized and atomic carbon, and carbon in its molecular form in CO. [CII] emission is the most extended, permeates the mapped region and is dynamically complex, while 13CO is compact and quiescent, and 12CO and [CI] occupy intermediate regimes connecting dense regions to transitional diffuse layers. We interpret these emission distributions such that the brightest [CII] emission traces photodissociation regions (PDRs) close to the H II region bubbles located along the central filament, while the extended [CII] emission arises from the more diffuse warm gas, indicating either cloud formation or dispersal processes. Remarkably, the [CI] is more extended than the 13CO, but less than [CII] and may probe the gas velocity structure resulting from colliding flows or cloud-cloud collisions. Line ratios involving [CII], such as [CII]/[CI] or [CII]/CO are systematically high, revealing widespread diffuse emission and localized UV-illuminated surfaces. Line ratio analysis and K-means clustering of [CI]/13CO versus dust continuum (cold 870 micron and warm 70 micron) emission reveal stratified chemical structure that UV photons penetrate deeply into the clumpy ridge (Av~18), suggesting a porous PDR. These results together depict that NGC 6334 is a clumpy, feedback-dominated PDR ridge with coexisting carbon phases, where [CI] and [CII] also trace dynamical processing through multiple velocity components linked to cloud-cloud collisions.

papers.title: Lessons from double-plane lenses for galaxy profiles, the Hubble tension, and the mass-sheet degeneracy
papers.authors: Daniel P. Johnson, Martin Millon, Pierre Fleury, Giacomo Queirolo, Tian Li, Wolfgang J. R. Enzi, Daniel J. Ballard, Duncan Bowden, Thomas E. Collett, Daniel Gilman
papers.abstract: Double-plane lenses, like single-plane lenses, are subject to the mass-sheet degeneracy, a fundamental limit to our knowledge of the deflector mass profiles from lensing. However, with a prior on the relative expansion history, unlike in the single-plane case, this degeneracy can be constrained with the modelling of lens images, without the need for time delays, velocity dispersion measurements or a prior on the Hubble constant $H_0$. We show that double-plane lenses are sensitive to a specific combination of the mass-sheet components of the two lens planes. Using literature values of the cosmological scaling factor from the double-plane lenses J0946 and AGEL0353, a measurement from the point-source images of J1721 (the ``Einstein zig-zag'' lens), and a reference value of $Ω_\mathrm{m}$, we show the constraints that can be placed on the mass-sheet component of each of these systems. We show that the additional information brought by images of a second source can improve measurements of $H_0$ from individual time-delay lenses by up to $\sim50\%$, depending on certain key assumptions. Using forecasted Euclid and LSST double-plane lens samples, we show that these samples will enable strong constraints on the population of mass sheets in lens galaxies. Such population constraints will have implications for a range of strong-lensing science applications, in particular in constraining $H_0$, dark energy, and the dark matter profiles of galaxies.

papers.title: The AIDA-TNG project: Galactic bar pattern speeds in self-interacting dark matter
papers.authors: Asiyeh Habibi, Mahmood Roshan, Giulia Despali, Mark Vogelsberger, Amir Ghari, Lauro Moscardini
papers.abstract: Cosmological simulations within the standard cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm systematically predict higher values of the dimensionless bar-speed parameter, $\boldsymbol{R} \equiv R_{\mathrm{cr}}/R_{\mathrm{bar}}$ (where $R_{\mathrm{cr}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{bar}}$ denote the corotation radius and the bar radius, respectively), than those inferred from observations of local galaxies, a discrepancy known as the fast-bar tension. Since bar slowdown is primarily driven by dynamical friction with the dark matter halo, bar dynamics is inherently sensitive to the properties of dark matter particles. We aim to determine whether dark matter self-interactions alleviate or exacerbate the fast-bar tension, and to identify the physical mechanism behind the differences in bar dynamics between CDM and self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models. We use the $51.7\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ box of the AIDA-TNG cosmological simulations, run with three different dark matter models: standard CDM, and two SIMD models one with a constant cross-section model (SIDM1), and the other with a velocity-dependent model (vSIDM). We identify barred disk galaxies with stellar mass $M_* > 10^{10}\,M_{\odot}$ at redshifts $z=0.2,\,1.0,\,1.5,$ and $2.0$, and measure the bar fraction, bar strength, bar length, pattern speed $Ω_{\mathrm{p}}$, and the ratio $\boldsymbol{R}=R_{\mathrm{cr}}/R_{\mathrm{bar}}$. The pattern speeds in the SIDM1 and vSIDM models are generally lower than in CDM at nearly all redshifts probed in this study. The subsequent slowdown proceeds with nearly 10\% more effective in the SIDM models likely due to velocity-anisotropy. Consequently, at low redshift the mean value of $\boldsymbol{R}$ is significantly higher in the SIDM models, indicating that the fas-bar tension is further exacerbated in these scenarios.

papers.title: Ensemble Individual Mode Frequency Modeling of Kepler Giants - Extending the IACgrid towards the red-giant branch
papers.authors: D. H. Grossmann, S. Mathur, P. G. Beck, D. Godoy-Rivera, B. Liagre, R. A. Garcia, L. S. Schimak, D. B. Palakkatharappil, M. H. Pinsonneault, F. Perez Hernandez
papers.abstract: Precise stellar parameters, in particular ages, are vital for understanding the formation and history of the Milky Way. Usually, this is achieved by fitting stellar evolution models to observational constraints such as spectroscopic and astrometric parameters. Adding global asteroseismic properties to the classical parameters (global seismic modeling) breaks some degeneracies and improves the results. However, this approach has its limitations, with red-giant random age uncertainties usually $\sim$ 20-50%, and often lacking proper quantification of the systematics. We aim to extend seismic modeling to include individual mode frequencies for red-giant branch stars, increasing the number of evolved solar-like oscillators with precise stellar parameters (ages, masses, and radii), and allowing us to quantify the systematics in global seismic modeling. We developed a grid of stellar evolutionary models and computed the individual oscillation frequencies, including a figure of merit to find the best-fitting model. We validate our methodology on a sample of red giants with individual frequency modeling from the literature, finding our masses, radii, and ages in close agreement. We then apply our method to around 100 Kepler red-giant branch stars of near-solar mass and metallicity, which previously have only been modeled with global seismic parameters. We obtain random average uncertainties of 3.4%, 1.3%, and 13.2%, for stellar masses, radii, and ages, respectively. We find that ages from individual mode frequency modeling are significantly, 14% on average, larger than those from global seismic mass-constrained modeling. The modeled luminosities agree within 1.0% with those derived from Gaia parallaxes. We conclude that modeling individual mode frequencies improves age precision by a factor of two for red-giant branch stars, providing stronger constraints for galactic archaeology.

papers.title: Odd Loops: What Structures Can Produce a Parity-Violating Inflationary Trispectrum?
papers.authors: William Ortolá Leonard, Zachary Slepian
papers.abstract: Non-Gaussian perturbations generated during inflation can often be described perturbatively via integrals of kernels acting on Gaussian fields. In this work, we investigate, in a model-independent manner, whether these kernels can produce parity-violating (PV) contributions to the trispectrum, and which Wick's theorem contraction configurations of the Gaussian fields lead to them. In detail, we evaluate all possible contraction configurations arising from the third- and second-order density perturbations. We find that, for the third-order perturbations, only one configuration can support PV contributions, as it retains three independent wave-vectors. In contrast, none of the four second-order perturbation contraction configurations can produce a PV contribution under statistical isotropy. These results offer a first step toward deriving kernels from inflationary models capable of generating a PV trispectrum. Such kernels could then be used to perform PV searches with current and upcoming galaxy redshift surveys such as DESI, Roman, SPHEREx, and Euclid, and photometric efforts such as LSST. Our results also offer a guide for exploration of PV with CMB data-sets such as Planck.

papers.title: Effects of a Nuclear Detonation in Low Earth Orbit
papers.authors: Zachary Petersen, Hong Qin, Sarah Thiele, Sébastien Philippe
papers.abstract: More than 13,000 satellites operate in low Earth orbit (LEO), and concern has grown that nuclear weapons could be used in space to target them. Beyond the initial X-ray burst, electrons released by radioactive fission products can become trapped in Earth's magnetic field, repeatedly exposing satellites as an artificial radiation belt. Here we couple prompt radiation, electron trapping and belt evolution to satellite failures, collisions and atmospheric drag. For a 1-Mt detonation at 500km over the South Atlantic, repeated belt exposure disables approximately 98% of modeled satellites within one week in our central case. Tripling the assumed radiation tolerance delays widespread failure by only days: approximately 97% are still disabled within two weeks. The loss of maneuverability sharply increases collision risk, with approximately 20 collisions expected within two years. Drag removes many disabled spacecraft from lower altitudes, but replacement satellites could remain exposed to radiation and debris for years. These findings show how a single detonation could devastate orbital infrastructure and support efforts to prevent the deployment and use of nuclear weapons in space.

papers.title: Superorbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
papers.authors: Abhisek Tamang, Hemanth Manikantan, Kinjal Roy, Ajith Balu, Biswajit Paul
papers.abstract: Context. Hercules X-1 (Her X-1) is a well-studied X-ray binary exhibiting superorbital modulation of its X-ray flux. The origin of this periodicity remains debated between a counter-precessing twisted-tilted accretion disc and free precession of the neutron star. Earlier observations (1970-1990) reported stochastic fluctuations in the superorbital period, with no long-term trend. Aims. We investigated the long-term trend of the superorbital modulation using more recent, uninterrupted data from 1995-2025 to identify features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. Methods. We probed the superorbital period using long-term light curves from five X-ray monitors, namely CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, and MAXI/GSC, together with literature data spanning $\sim$50 yr. We employed multiple timing analysis tools to trace its evolution. Results. The uninterrupted data from the last 30 years show that the superorbital period is decreasing at a rate of $\sim -5 \times 10^{-5}$ s s$^{-1}$. The $O-C$ analysis reveals shorter-timescale variability superimposed on the overall decay; thus, a simple quadratic function cannot explain the observed $O-C$ variations. We also find a positive correlation between the mean count rate and superorbital period across different linear segments of the $O-C$ curve. Conclusions. Period variations over a few to a few tens of superorbital cycles suggest a restoring mechanism in the system. We discuss possible mechanisms responsible for the observed long-term decay and short-term variability. (Abbreviated.)

papers.title: Does DESI point towards transient cosmic acceleration?
papers.authors: Muhammad Ahmad, Saddam Hussain, Ayodeji Ibitoye, Yi'an Zhao, Ming Zhang, Lang Cui
papers.abstract: We investigate an oscillatory equation of state for dark energy that oscillates around the mean value $-1$ and includes a source term proportional to the cube of the number of e-folds. Due to this source term, the oscillation amplitude shifts towards the $w_{\rm de}<-1$ regime at higher redshifts, whereas in the future, the source term drives the oscillation amplitude towards the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime. As the equation of state enters the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime in the future, the dark energy density dilutes, causing the Hubble parameter to decrease asymptotically towards zero, so that the present acceleration is transient: the Universe transitions to decelerated expansion and approaches a static state as $a\to\infty$, without ever contracting. We compare this equation of state with BellDE, CPL and flat $Λ$CDM. We confront the model with a combination of datasets, including Planck, DESI BAO and three different supernova compilations: Pantheon+, Union3 and DES-Dovekie. We compare the log-evidence of each model with that of $Λ$CDM. The dynamical dark energy models yield $H_0$ values in the range $66.0^{+0.80}_{-0.79}$--$67.84^{+0.69}_{-0.74}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, with matter density values in the range $Ω_{\rm m}=0.3067^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072}$--$0.3271^{+0.0083}_{-0.0080}$ across all the combinations. These values are consistent with those of the baseline model, apart from a mild upward shift in $Ω_{\rm m}$ for the Union3 combination. Among all the models, BellDE yields comparatively stronger Bayesian evidence than the other models, with weak evidence for the Pantheon+ compilation and moderate evidence for the Union3 and DES-Dovekie compilations. The sourced oscillatory model yields inconclusive evidence for Pantheon + and Union3, while weak evidence for DES-Dovekie relative to $Λ$CDM.

papers.title: Forecasting Fundamental-Plane Tests of Intermediate-mass Black Holes in Radio-selected Dwarf Galaxies
papers.authors: Ramananda Santra, Samik Mitra, Shahram Abbassi
papers.abstract: A radio/X-ray Fundamental Plane (FP) test of an intermediate-mass black hole is informative only when the compact radio emission, hard X-rays, accretion state, and host association refer to the same accretor. We used published VLA, VLBA, \textit{Chandra}, and \textit{HST} observations of a radio-selected dwarf-galaxy sample to determine when present nondetections are constraining and what observations are required for a stronger test. The VLBA follow-up reveals that compactness alone does not establish association with the target dwarf, while for the best nuclear candidates the radio component relevant to the FP has not yet been isolated on the intermediate physical scales between the VLA and VLBA measurements. We therefore recast the FP as a forward question: for an assumed black-hole mass, how likely is a given radio observation to detect the compact core? The calculation includes intrinsic FP scatter, X-ray uncertainties, the radio spectral index, the accretion state, and source size relative to the beam. The existing VLBA nondetections have low completeness across the adopted intermediate-mass range and do not provide useful black-hole mass upper limits. Meaningful tests require deeper resolution-matched radio imaging, recovery of intermediate-scale structure, and contemporaneous measurements of the intrinsic hard-X-ray component. Because the calculation returns a mass-dependent detection function for each source, the same framework can be applied to larger dwarf-galaxy samples to quantify survey completeness and build selection functions for population studies of low-mass black holes.

papers.title: Advances in High-Precision Astrometry for Exoplanet Detection for Astrometric Missions
papers.authors: Fabien Malbet, Jerôme Amiaux, Florence Ardellier-Desages, Eric Doumayrou, Pierre-Antoine Frugier, Pierre-Olivier Lagage, Alain Léger, Manon Lizzana, Jérôme Martignac, Julien Michelot, Fabrice Pancher, Thibault Pichon, Samuel Ronayette, Hugo Rousset, Sebastien Soler, Eric Thiébaut
papers.abstract: High-precision astrometry is a cornerstone for detecting Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars and probing the nature of dark matter in galactic environments. Achieving sub-microarcsecond accuracy requires unprecedented control over detector morphology, optical distortion, and astrometric measurement techniques. This paper reviews recent progress in characterizing large format detector at the micropixel scale level, calibrating optical distortion using reference stars, and refining differential astrometry methods to detect the faint astrometric signatures of Earth-mass exoplanets. We highlight the latest developments in the RETINA project, which aims to advance the TRL of GIGAPYX 220 MP CMOS detectors from Pyxalis which are critical components for future space missions such as ESA's Theia and NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The project focuses on precise calibration methods, including Young's fringe projection, to monitor pixel geometry and intra-pixel response across gigapixel-scale focal planes. By integrating these advancements, RETINA seeks to enable astrometric detection of Earth-mass exoplanets with a precision of few tens of micropixels on the focal plane. We discuss the technical strategies, laboratory validations, and system-level integration required to achieve these goals, emphasizing the synergy between detector technology, optical calibration, and mission design. These innovations pave the way for next-generation astrometric instruments capable of transforming our understanding of exoplanetary systems and dark matter dynamics.

papers.title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
papers.authors: Pei Jin, Mariano Méndez, Federico García, Diego Altamirano, Haifan Zhu, Liang Zhang, Guobao Zhang
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black-hole X-ray binaries show nonlinear coupling with broadband variability, producing characteristic ridge, hypotenuse, and web-like structures in the bicoherence. However, the origin of these structures remains unclear. We develop a mathematical model in which a modulator phase-locked to the QPO acts multiplicatively on the underlying variability. The resulting frequency mixing naturally produces both the ridge and hypotenuse associated with the fundamental QPO, as two parts of the same modulation-induced bispectral structure, and the same mechanism extends to the second harmonic. The model further predicts opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. We test these predictions using NICER observations of Swift~J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI~J1820$+$070. The bispectral maps show QPO-related ridge--hypotenuse structures broadly consistent with the model, with qualitatively opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. In particular, the biphase map provides a complementary diagnostic that reveals weak coupling structures that are difficult to identify from the bicoherence alone. We also compare the measured bispectral modulus with the predictions for isolated ridges and hypotenuses. These predictions broadly reproduce the observed frequency dependence, while localized deviations remain near the fundamental-QPO and second-harmonic frequencies, where different bispectral structures overlap. Our results provide a simple mathematical framework in which the web-like pattern in the bispectrum could arise naturally from multiplicative coupling between a QPO-phase-locked modulator and the underlying variability.

papers.title: Fundamental Noise Processes in Pulsar Timing
papers.authors: James M. Cordes, Stella Koch Ocker, Shami Chatterjee, Timothy Dolch, Ross J. Jennings, Michael T. Lam, Jacob E. Turner
papers.abstract: The stability of spin rates and emission regions of radio-emitting neutron stars (pulsars) has enabled remarkable advances, including the detection of exoplanets, testing theories of gravity, and stimulating the vigorous exploration of a new window in gravitational wave astronomy an nanohertz frequencies. An ideal astrophysical clock would emit identical pulses at a constant rate, propagating along single geodesics through a perfect vacuum. In reality, the timing precision achievable with pulsars is limited by spin noise, variability in the beam produced in a complex magnetosphere, and multipath propagation through a turbulent interstellar medium, with additional limitations from uncertainties in the changing pulsar -- observatory vector and instrumental effects. Here we present the fundamentals of pulsar timing, its current limitations, and prospects for improvements in timing precision. We develop metrics to assess the timing quality of a pulsar and use them to evaluate sources currently included in pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) as a means for characterizing the quality of future pulsar discoveries. With increases in telescope sensitivity, pulsar timing precision will increasingly be limited by propagation effects in the interstellar medium. We identify sources of non-Gaussianity in timing residuals and separate out effects that are chromatic or achromatic, as well as effects that vary on short (seconds to minutes) and longer (days to months) timescales. Modern wide-bandwidth receivers provide simultaneous arrival times across a range of frequencies, enabling the robust mitigation of chromatic interstellar effects and the identification of non-Gaussian events superimposed on random fluctuations. We recommend changes to timing procedures that leverage instrumentation advances to improve timing precision.

papers.title: SQUALO II: Probing Accretion Through CO Molecular Outflows in Massive Star-forming Clumps
papers.authors: S. Mercimek, G. A. Fuller, A. Traficante, T. Pillai, A. Nucara, W. -A. Chen, D. Walker, L. Testi, M. Benedettini
papers.abstract: Molecular outflows probe protostellar accretion and mass transfer from clump scales to forming stars. We present an ALMA study of CO (J=2-1) outflows toward 13 massive clumps from the SQUALO sample, spanning a broad evolutionary range and exhibiting clump-scale infall. We identify 51 high-velocity CO lobes associated with 31 outflow systems and derive their physical and dynamical properties assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium. Outflow inferred accretion rates are typically 10^{-5}-10^{-3} Msun/yr, consistent with active massive star formation. The maximum outflow velocity shows little dependence on candidate driving-core mass, indicating that it is not a reliable tracer of protostellar mass in clustered environments. Outflow momentum flux correlates positively with clump surface density, whereas accretion rate shows a tentative, statistically nonsignificant decrease with increasing virial parameter. Total outflow inferred accretion rate shows a tentative positive relation with clump-scale infall rate but remains systematically lower, suggesting that the detected outflows represent only part of the large-scale mass flux. The clump L/M ratio moderately anticorrelates with projected outflow length, although projection, observational limitations, and the embedded source population prevent a unique evolutionary interpretation. Together with the continuum derived fragmentation properties, our results show that compact cores embedded within infalling clumps drive the outflows. The tentative relation between clump-scale infall and protostellar accretion suggests a possible connection across these scales, although our observations do not directly trace mass transfer from filaments to individual protostars.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of BDNK hydrodynamics: from heavy-ion collisions to astrophysics
papers.authors: Teerthal Patel, Henry V. Hirvonen, Fábio S. Bemfica, Marcelo M. Disconzi, Jorge Noronha, Jean-François Paquet
papers.abstract: We present new developments in the mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of the causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamic theory by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK) in general spacetimes. We develop two independent flux-conservative algorithms for arbitrary 3+1-dimensional spacetime metrics. Both are hyperbolic, causal, and well-posed, pass convergence tests, and reproduce known results. The first uses a new first-order reduction with mathematically preserved constraints, whose numerical violations can be handled with cleaning fields (the resulting coupled system is proven hyperbolic and well-posed). The second uses a new mixed-order formulation, whose solutions are proven strictly equivalent to the original BDNK system, without cleaning fields. Our proofs rely on a new general theorem providing sufficient conditions for transforming a mixed-order system with arbitrary-order equations into a strictly hyperbolic system, strengthening a classical result by Choquet Bruhat for weak hyperbolicity. We introduce a new practical prescription for selecting admissible hydrodynamic frames for a broad class of equations of state, including nonconformal ones relevant to heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics. Our simulations capture viscous shock broadening and suppression of Kelvin--Helmholtz vortices, reproduce Bjorken and Gubser flows, and study departures from stationary ideal-fluid configurations in Michel accretion and rotating tori on fixed Schwarzschild and Kerr backgrounds. For heavy-ion collisions, we perform boost invariant simulations with a lattice-QCD-based equation of state and fluctuating TRENTo initial conditions, comparing BDNK with a minimal Israel--Stewart theory. The descriptions agree at small shear viscosity but can differ substantially at larger viscosities, particularly for early initialization with rapid longitudinal expansion.

papers.title: XMM-Newton observations of the highest field polar AR UMa: An extreme case of soft-blobby accretion
papers.authors: Kala G. Pradeep, Axel D. Schwope
papers.abstract: (Context) The X-ray spectra of magnetic cataclysmic variables (MCVs) with extreme magnetic fields, the polars, often exhibit a prominent soft X-ray excess attributed to buried shocks. (Aims) Using the first-ever high-state XMM-Newton observation of the highest field polar, AR UMa ($B\approx230$ MG), we established the source's accretion scenario and derived the energy budget at the magnetic extreme of MCVs. (Methods) Using X-ray, UV, and optical spectral and timing analysis, we disentangled the radiation components and located their origin in the binary. (Results) AR UMa showed one active ("southern") pole during our observation. The spectrum of the active pole was dominated by soft, blackbody-like emission with $kT_{\rm BB} \simeq 35$ eV and showed no evidence for an optically thin hard X-ray emission characteristic of a cooling post-shock accretion column. Instead, we find constant, faint, optically thin plasma emission with a temperature of $\approx 1$ keV at all orbital phases, which is uncorrelated with the soft X-ray emission, and we attribute this to shock-heated matter at the stagnation region. Pronounced absorption dips punctuate the phase of active X-ray emission and are associated with puffed-up material in the stagnation region. Using spectro-timing analysis of the absorption dips, the density profile and evolution of the clumpy flow were probed. We find evidence of a cyclotron harmonic from the southern pole (160 MG) near $\sim$2300 Angstrom in the UV spectrum. We report minute-long quasi-periodic oscillations in the optical, UV, and X-ray light curves. (Conclusion) AR UMa represents an extreme case of soft, blobby accretion, with an effectively infinite soft excess, extending the magnetic field range over which magnetic accretion can be studied by a factor of two. It is one of the rare systems in which X-ray emission from a stream-magnetosphere interaction is detected.

papers.title: A joint astrometric, eclipse timing and radial velocity orbit for the hierarchical triple V819 Herculis
papers.authors: Furkan Akar, Özgür Baştürk
papers.abstract: We present a joint Bayesian orbital analysis of the hierarchical triple system V819 Herculis using ground-based astrometry, radial velocities (RV), and eclipse timing variations (ETV). By coupling these complementary data sets within a physically consistent Keplerian framework, we obtain a self-consistent three-dimensional solution for the outer orbit and the dynamical properties of the system. The outer orbit is found to have a period of $P_3 = 2016.97 \pm 0.27$ d and a high eccentricity of $e_3 = 0.6800 \pm 0.0016$, with the same orbital geometry simultaneously reproducing the sky-plane astrometry, the LiTE signal in the eclipse timings, and the tertiary radial velocities. The joint solution determines the component masses dynamically from these data alone, yielding $M_{12} = 2.721 \pm 0.055\,M_\odot$ for the inner binary and $M_3 = 1.954 \pm 0.070\,M_\odot$ for the tertiary, together with a LiTE amplitude of $A_\mathrm{LiTE} = 0.0104$ d and an RV semi-amplitude of $K_3 = 18.46$ km s$^{-1}$. The joint fit also yields an orbital parallax of $π_\mathrm{orb} = 14.08 \pm 0.13$ mas, consistent with Gaia DR3, Gaia DR2 and the HIPPARCOS New Reduction. The derived tertiary mass is higher than expected for a standard G8-type main-sequence star, suggesting that the tertiary component may be in an advanced evolutionary stage. The resulting outer orbit is well constrained, and the system is strongly hierarchical, with an outer period about 900 times the inner one. Finally, we provide predicted astrometric positions for the tertiary component for five years beyond 2026.5 to guide future high-precision observations.

papers.title: Through Ups and Downs: the Transient Lensing Behaviour of SIDM halos undergoing Core Collapse
papers.authors: Frank C. van den Bosch, Yarone M. Tokayer
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes can become extremely dense following gravothermal core collapse, motivating their use as explanations for unusually concentrated gravitational lenses. Using an emulator calibrated on gravothermal fluid calculations, we investigate whether increasing central density necessarily strengthens lensing. We follow initially Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) haloes through core formation and collapse deep into the short-mean-free-path regime, and compute finite-source magnifications, critical curves, and source-plane lensing cross sections for isolated spherical haloes with elastic, velocity-independent self-interactions, including external shear in selected calculations. Lensing strength evolves non-monotonically: it initially decreases during core formation, rises during early collapse, and generally declines at later stages despite continued growth of the central density. This decline accompanies the emergence of a dense inner core whose mass and radius decrease within a more extended, lower-density core. Time-averaged enhancement relative to NFW haloes depends on the lensing statistic, halo concentration, and interaction cross section. Generalized NFW haloes with central cusps $ρ\propto r^{-γ}$ with $γ\geq 2$ always have larger lensing efficacies than core-collapsed SIDM haloes of equal mass and are therefore poor proxies, including in terms of the demographics (size and radial thickness) of arcs and Einstein rings. The core collapse stage at which SIDM haloes are optimal lenses coincides with the epoch at which the characteristic core surface density is close to critical, which typically occurs during the early stages of core collapse. These results demonstrate that central density alone is insufficient to characterize SIDM lensing and that its evolving mass distribution must be modelled explicitly.

papers.title: Violent relaxation redux
papers.authors: Michael L. Nastac, Yonadav Barry Ginat, Robert J. Ewart, Michael Barnes, Alexander A. Schekochihin
papers.abstract: Collisionless self-gravitating systems, such as merging galaxies, have long seemed an exception to the statistical-mechanical principle that chaotic many-body systems relax to maximum-entropy states: Lynden-Bell's statistical mechanics of their "violent relaxation," constrained by exact conservation of phase-space volume -- equivalently, of infinitely many collisionless "Casimir" invariants -- has appeared not to be a good description. We propose that violent relaxation does give rise to Lynden-Bell's maximum-entropy equilibria, but that both are underpinned by gravitational turbulence, in which large-scale gravitational fluctuations drive chaotic phase-space mixing of the particles' distribution function. We derive the universal small-scale (sub-Jeans) spectra of this turbulence and show that it leads to phase-space-volume conservation being broken on a timescale only logarithmically longer, in the particle number N, than the dynamical (violent-relaxation) time. This timescale separation lets the system relax "adiabatically" through a sequence of Lynden-Bell equilibria, each corresponding to instantaneous values of the Casimirs. At long times, it approaches an equilibrium close to its "ground state": a distribution whose Casimirs have adjusted so that the system's energy is now its minimum possible energy. Thus, the system's universal tendency is toward a minimum-energy, maximum-entropy state. We corroborate this picture with 1D N-body simulations and hypothesize that it can explain the universal equilibria of galaxies and dark-matter halos.

papers.title: Constraints on Cosmic-Rays and the MeV Emission from Jupiter's Atmosphere
papers.authors: Dimitris Tsatsis, Thomas Siegert, Volodymyr Savchenko, Saurabh Mittal, Laura Eisenberger, Mika A. Gelowicz, Rudi Reinhardt, Manja L. Zimmerer, Tristan Bouchet, Tomohiko Oka, Manuel R. H. W. Skalka
papers.abstract: The Cosmic $γ$-ray Background (CGB) in the MeV regime remains among the least understood components of diffuse cosmic radiation, primarily due to instrumental limitations in detecting faint isotropic emission at MeV energies. We present an indirect method for probing isotropic emission from soft X-rays to $γ$-rays through scattered emission in Jupiter's atmosphere. Using archival observations from SPI, the spectrometer aboard INTEGRAL, spanning 22 years of serendipitous Jupiter observations, we analyse the planet as a moving $γ$-ray point source in the 30 keV to 8 MeV range. Our analysis focuses on Jupiter's $γ$-ray albedo, produced by high-energy photon and cosmic-ray interactions. We performed detailed Monte Carlo simulations to model the response of Jupiter's atmosphere to incident photons, protons, electrons, positrons, and alpha particles. We simulate a 1000 km deep spherical atmosphere with 1 km shell resolution, based on Galileo probe measurements. By comparing empirical and astrophysical models with the SPI data, we find no statistically significant emission from Jupiter. We derive $2σ$ upper limits across the 30 keV to 8 MeV band, which we compare with cutoff power-law, reflected CGB, cosmic-ray-induced, and long-lived mediator dark matter models. We constrain Jupiter's bremsstrahlung luminosity in the MeV range to $10^{18}$ erg/s, close to that inferred from in situ measurements obtained by Juno/JEDI. While the expected emission from the CGB and cosmic rays is a factor of $10^4$ and 100 below our upper limits, respectively, this work establishes planetary atmospheres as promising indirect probes of diffuse $γ$-ray backgrounds for future MeV missions.

papers.title: Validation of Habitable Zone Limits with a New Radiative-Convective Equilibrium Climate Model
papers.authors: Jacob Haqq-Misra, Eric T. Wolf, Ravi K. Kopparapu
papers.abstract: The habitable zone (HZ) boundaries calculated with the Clima one-dimensional radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) model have served as a standard reference for exoplanet target selection for three decades, but they have never been independently validated with a comparable model. We present ExoColumn, a new one-dimensional RCE model that couples an independently developed atmospheric column physics package to the ExoRT correlated-k radiative transfer core that is also used by the three-dimensional ExoCAM model. We calibrate ExoColumn to present-day conditions, which matches other RCE models to within a few kelvin through the troposphere. Line-by-line benchmarks show that the ExoRT and Clima radiation cores each reproduce the outgoing longwave flux to within a few percent, with the differences due to the spectral line databases used by each model. We follow the same inverse climate modeling method as previous studies have done to find inner edge moist- and runaway-greenhouse limits of 0.970 au and 0.966 au, and an outer-edge maximum-greenhouse limit of 1.611 au at a CO$_2$ partial pressure of 8.7 bar. We extend these calculations to 12 host stars spanning 2000-7200 K and to planets of 0.1, 1, and 5 Earth mass, and we provide updated HZ boundary coefficients for community use. The ExoColumn limits systematically fall closer to the host star than those of Clima but agree to within a few percent in orbital distance, which validates the robustness of the published Clima HZ boundaries.

papers.title: CO gaps in cold transition disks around low-mass stars
papers.authors: A. A. Rota, N. van der Marel, E. F. van Dishoeck, T. Muto
papers.abstract: Transition disks with large inner dust cavities are promising targets to study planet formation, as these disks are likely hosting massive planetary companions. The structure of gas and dust inside the cavity are crucial for understanding the potential of planet formation in the regions. We investigate the structure of gas and dust in a sample of three cold, inclined transition disks around K and M stars without evidence for an inner dusty disk. We present new high-resolution ALMA Band 6 data of both 230 GHz continuum at 0.02" (~3 au) resolution and the 12CO 2-1, 13CO 2-1, C18O 2-1 isotopologues at 0.12" (~20 au) resolution. We analyze the radial profiles, compute the brightness temperatures, and derive estimates of the gas and dust content of the inner disk at 1 au. All three disks show dust cavities of 30-40 au in radius. The CO emission extends inside the cavity with progressively smaller CO cavity radii for the more abundant isotopologues. The 13CO brightness temperature profile is similar to that of other transition disks and full disks. No inner dust disk is detected in the ALMA continuum, consistent with the lack of near-infrared excess. Considering the accretion rates, the gas-to-dust ratio in the inner disk at 1 au is estimated to be as high as 10^5. No significant differences in the brightness temperature or in the gas-to-dust ratio are found between our disks and other transition disks around more luminous stars, contrary to expectations. This highlights the importance of individual-target studies through thermochemical modeling or multi-transition analyses to constrain the dust and gas structures in the cavity. The observed disk structures could be explained by super-Jovian companion on eccentric orbits, but further modeling is needed to confirm this conclusion.

papers.title: Where the red rise stops: JWST/MIRI reveals a near-infrared turnover in the Little Red Dot Abell2744-QSO1
papers.authors: E. Iani, P. Rinaldi, A. Torralba, J. Matthee, F. D'Eugenio, A. Gupta, S. Mascia, C. Di Cesare, G. Oestlin, G. Kotiwale, M. Catone, G. Rodighiero
papers.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact sources with a blue rest-frame UV, a steep red optical continuum and, often, broad hydrogen lines. They have been interpreted as dense stellar systems, dust-reddened active galactic nuclei, or black holes embedded in dense, dust-poor gas, scenarios that are hard to tell apart in the rest-frame UV and optical. We present JWST/MIRI F770W and F1000W imaging of the triply lensed Abell2744-QSO1 at z=7.04, probing rest-frame 0.96 and 1.24um. QSO1 is unresolved, and its steep optical rise stops near rest-frame 1um. Up to 1.24um, a T~4450K blackbody, or a hotter one reddened by dust, describes the continuum, with no sign of the hot dust seen in most type-1 quasars. Our statistically preferred SED fits produce the red continuum with (3-4)x10^9 Msun of stars, over 100 times the dynamical limit on the host mass, and are therefore disfavoured. An accretion disc in a dense gas cocoon respects this limit but over-predicts the 1.24um flux by 5 sigma. Super-Eddington accretion models with a thermalising envelope reproduce the turnover, but only for a black hole ~2.5dex less massive than the dynamical estimate. For a dust-reddened accretion disc (A_V ~ 2 mag), dust at ~1200K can re-emit at most ~2 per cent of the absorbed luminosity, and most of it would have to emerge at ~70-600K, unless the dust covers only a small fraction of the sky. The dynamics favour an accretion-powered source, but our data cannot distinguish dust reddening from processing by dense gas. MIRI imaging at >18um could separate these scenarios.

papers.title: The OpenMULTI3D stellar analysis package. A 3D non-LTE spectrum synthesis code for AFGKM-type stars within the DISPATCH framework
papers.authors: Richard Hoppe, Maria Bergemann, Philipp Eitner, Åke Nordlund, Jorrit Leenaarts, Andrius Popovas, Nicholas Storm
papers.abstract: Upcoming large spectroscopic surveys such as WEAVE, 4MOST, and SDSS-V will provide millions of high-resolution stellar spectra. This motivates the development of efficient codes to perform three-dimensional (3D) non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) radiative transfer (RT) calculations, in order to meet the requirements on efficiency and data analysis quality set by these surveys. We present a new open access 3D non-LTE spectrum synthesis code OpenMULTI3D, based on its predecessor MULTI3D, which was never released. This code can be used to compute large grids of spectra of AFGKM-type stars and will aid the exploitation of large-scale spectroscopic surveys such as 4MOST. We summarise the main input micro- and macro-physics of the code, describe its numerical implementation and provide selected test cases. The outputs of the code are compared with standard results in the literature, including the NLTE departure coefficients in 1D and 3D, the 3D NLTE abundance corrections, 3D synthetic spectral energy distributions for three types of stars, and 3D NLTE Balmer-line profiles of a metal-poor red giant. We also demonstrate how the code can be used to compute time-dependent spectra of stars, which may be relevant in precision stellar physics and analyses of exoplanet spectra. OpenMULTI3D offers an accessible and efficient platform for high-fidelity stellar analysis in the era of large-scale spectroscopic surveys.

papers.title: Primordial non-Gaussianity as a large-scale cosmic-web bias
papers.authors: Kilian Peraza Vera, Francisco-Shu Kitaura, Francesco Sinigaglia
papers.abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity is a unique probe of the physics of inflation, but its large-scale-structure signature is difficult to measure because it appears on the largest, most cosmic-variance-limited modes. The standard view of local-type primordial non-Gaussianity is isotropic: it induces a scale-dependent correction to tracer bias, $Δb(k)\propto f_{\rm NL}k^{-2}$, on large scales. Here we show that the same large-scale response can be reformulated as an anisotropic, nonlocal environmental-bias effect. Motivated by the spectral cosmic-web hierarchy of Kitaura and Sinigaglia, we define a Hessian field $\mathcal{H}_{ij}(\bf{x})\equiv\partial_i\partial_j\nabla^{-4}δ(\bf{x})$, whose trace obeys $\mathrm{Tr}\mathcal{H}=\nabla^{-2}δ$ and therefore carries the same $k^{-2}$ enhancement that appears in the Dalal et al. scale-dependent-bias term. Diagonalizing $\mathcal{H}_{ij}$ defines four large-scale web environments, analogous to knots, filaments, sheets, and voids, although operating on scales much larger than the conventional nonlinear cosmic web. We assign one weight to each environment and test the construction with the AbacusPNG suite of local-PNG $N$-body simulations, using $f_{\rm NL}=\{-100,-30,30,100\}$. We show that these four weights reproduce the large-scale $k^{-2}$ rise of the tracer bias. We further show that existing halo catalogs without PNG can be post-processed to imprint an effective $f_{\rm NL}$ signature. Beyond mock generation, the resulting cosmic-web response motivates an observational statistic based on changes in tracer occupation of large-scale environments relative to a matched Gaussian reference, complementary to the conventional low-$k$ power spectrum.

papers.title: Existence of Distinct Strong and Weak Shear Regimes of Self-Generated Turbulent Magnetic Reconnection
papers.authors: Qihui Ming, Alexander J. B. Russell
papers.abstract: Magnetic reconnection can become fast in three-dimensional turbulent layers. However, the parameters and mechanisms that control the fast state are not yet fully clear. Existing guide-field simulations of self-generated turbulent reconnection show locally coherent flux-rope structures embedded in a stochastic layer, motivating a flux-rope-mediated picture, with reconnection rates of order $V_{\rm rec}/V_A \sim 0.01$ in MHD. Here, we test whether and how magnetic shear changes the reconnection regime, using 3D resistive-MHD simulations at $S_L=10^5$. We vary the guide field while keeping the initial reconnecting field strength and rate normalization fixed, comparing a guide-field, weaker-shear configuration with the anti-parallel, strong-shear limit. We find that the strong-shear regime is qualitatively distinct from the flux-rope-mediated guide-field regime. Rather than retaining a narrow layer and locally coherent flux-rope structures, the current layer develops short-wavelength corrugations that broaden it substantially, and the reconnection layer electric field is sustained by fluctuation EMF. The reconnection rate increases to $V_{\rm rec}/V_A \sim 0.03$, about three times the guide-field value. These results indicate that magnetic shear can select the mechanism controlling fast 3D turbulent reconnection, shifting the system from a guide-field regime consistent with flux-rope mediation toward a very fast turbulence-broadened regime. This transition provides a novel explanation for the sudden switch-on of fast reconnection in eruptive solar flares.

papers.title: Activity of the ejected galactic nuclei and cosmic rays
papers.authors: Yu. N. Eroshenko
papers.abstract: The double and triple approaches of supermassive central black holes are a fairly common process in the hierarchical picture of galaxy formation. In this case, the ejection of a black hole is possible; it may carry the accretion disk and some amount of stars with it. The activity of the galactic nucleus can be restored after the ejection. One consequence of this activity is an ultrafast gas outflow, accompanied by a shock wave. We show that the acceleration of cosmic rays at such a shock is more effective than in the case of a stationary galactic nucleus due to the lower density of the surrounding gas and the higher velocity of the shock front. In this case, proton acceleration can occur up to energies of ~10^{19} eV, which is an order of magnitude higher than in an ordinary nucleus in the centers of galaxies.

papers.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
papers.authors: Bo Gao, Shao-Peng Tang, Yi-Zhong Fan, Qingzhong Liu
papers.abstract: Hierarchical triple mergers denote a sequential merger process in which the black hole remnant from an initial binary merger subsequently merges with a third black hole. In this study, we identify a related pair of binary black hole mergers, GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626, which exhibit consistent sky localization and luminosity distances; the latter is identified as a candidate hierarchical merger binary back holes. The Bayes factor in favor of a hierarchical triple merger origin over the non-association hypothesis is $110$. However, after accounting for the priors odds, the corresponding odds ratio decreases to $0.1$, indicating that the current evidence is insufficient to favor the hierarchical triple merger scenario. GW230720\_0823 show no detectable signatures of orbit eccentricity or line-of-sight acceleration. The inferred properties of these two gravitational wave events suggest a dynamical formation channel, such as few-body scattering or gas-assisted mergers, while a primordial triple origin is disfavored. Among the proposed dynamical environments, the accretion disk of an active galactic nucleus provides the most plausible site. We further derive constraints on the local rate of hierarchical triple mergers rate under both the null and candidate scenarios. Under the assumption of no detected hierarchical triple mergers, the most stringent $90\%$ confidence upper limit is $4.2\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ for $t_{\rm max}=10$ years using the GWTC-4 catalog.

papers.title: Successive Decimetric Bursts Associated with Breakout Magnetic Reconnection during the Decay Phase of an M-Class Flare
papers.authors: Suli Ma, Yihua Yan, Wei Wang, Hamish Reid, Ting Li, Xiaoshuai Zhu, Huadong Chen, Zhichao Zhou, Jing Huang, Linjie Chen, Chengming Tan, Xingyao Chen, Minghui Zhang, Xin Yao
papers.abstract: Radio imaging spectroscopy diagnoses coronal electron acceleration and propagation by tracking energetic electron beams and locating energy-release sites. Using MUSER (0.4-2 GHz) and SDO data, we investigate decimetric radio emission during an eruption with an M1.1 flare on 17 December 2014. The eruption involves a twisted coronal structure evolving through three stages: a violent internal eruption, a rise-and-expansion phase, and a breakout eruption. The flare peaks at 01:50 UT during the internal eruption, while the cluster of successive type III-like decimetric bursts occurs in the decay phase, linked to the breakout eruption. The radio source coincides with a high-squashing-factor Q region from nonlinear force-free field (NLFFF) extrapolations, indicating a quasi-separatrix layer (QSL). We interpret the radio emission as consistent with plasma emission driven by nonthermal electrons accelerated by breakout reconnection at this QSL, between the outer envelope of the erupting structure and the surrounding corona. The successive bursts occur in the decay phase because breakout reconnection involves a larger, more energetic twisted structure at higher altitude, where an extended high-Q region, favorable acceleration geometry, and repeated sub-eruptions sustain efficient electron acceleration. Missing soft X-ray enhancement suggests most accelerated electrons escape upward or lose energy before reaching the chromosphere. The concentrated source positions of the successive radio bursts suggest pseudostreamers may act as particle accelerators, trapping electrons and directing them along a narrow layer. These results establish decimetric radio imaging as a powerful diagnostic of breakout reconnection and particle acceleration in the solar corona, with implications for energy release in pseudostreamer environments.

papers.title: The N/O-O/H relation across large-scale environments
papers.authors: Yllari K. González-Koda, Almudena Zurita, Laura Sánchez-Menguiano, Ray Garner, Sebastián F. Sánchez, Bahar Bidaran, Estrella Florido, Mónica Relaño, Isabel Pérez, Simon Verley
papers.abstract: The large-scale structure (LSS) of the Universe shapes galaxy evolution through its intricate web-like morphology, yet its specific influence on gas-phase chemical abundances remains uncertain. Particularly, a homogeneous comparison of the N/O$-$O/H relation, a tracer of the mass assembly and baryonic cycle, across distinct LSS environments has been lacking. In this study, we analyse a local SDSS galaxy sample curated within the framework of the CAVITY project -- dedicated to studying void galaxies -- in which galaxies are classified by their LSS environment into three groups: clusters, voids, and non-cluster/non-void (NCNV). We extract spectroscopic emission line fluxes from the central SDSS spectra and analyse how different galaxy properties affect the scatter in the N/O$-$O/H relation. For that, we subtract the main N/O$-$O/H relation from the data and study the dependence of the resulting residuals ($ξ_\text{N/O}$) on a set of parameters, including stellar mass ($M_\star$), $g-r$ colour, and star formation rate (SFR). We find that $M_\star-$related variables are the best predictors of the scatter in the N/O$-$O/H relation, with little influence of the recent star formation history. Regarding the LSS comparison, no significant differences are found for void and NCNV galaxies. Cluster galaxies, however, present a N/O$-$O/H relation systematically lower (with $ξ_\text{N/O} \sim -0.02$). Consistent with this shift and with $M_\star$ as a good predictor of N/O$-$O/H deviations, we find that environmental dependences are also reflected in fundamental scaling relations: both the MZR and N/O$-M_\star$ relations are different for cluster galaxies. These combined results point to mechanisms in the dense intracluster medium (such as strangulation or re-accretion of metal-enriched gas) as the primary drivers of these chemical offsets for galaxies in cluster environments.

papers.title: Suppression of water-ice UV photodesorption on cosmic dust analogs
papers.authors: Ph. Parent, C. Laffon
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) photodesorption regulates the partitioning of water between interstellar ice mantles and the gas phase, yet laboratory yields are generally measured on planar substrates rather than on surfaces representative of cosmic dust. We investigate how grain morphology affects UV photodesorption from thin H$_2$O ice films of 2-6 monolayers deposited on planar gold and olivine, soot nanoparticles, and olivine microparticles. Samples were irradiated at 12 and 60 K with a microwave-discharge hydrogen lamp, and ice depletion was monitored by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and reflection-absorption infrared spectroscopy. On planar gold, the photodesorption yield increases approximately linearly with ice coverage, from $\sim5\times10^{-4}$ to $\sim2\times10^{-3}$ molecule photon$^{-1}$ between 2 and 6 monolayers, consistent with increasing UV absorption in optically thin ice; planar olivine gives comparable yields. In contrast, photodesorption is suppressed on particulate olivine and, more strongly, on soot, where yields are up to a factor of $\sim40$ lower than on gold at 12 K. Both experimental techniques confirm the strong suppression of ice depletion on soot. These results show that UV photodesorption depends not only on ice coverage but also strongly on grain morphology. The pronounced suppression on soot may reflect heterogeneous ice growth and altered energy redistribution within nanoscale ice domains, implying that yields measured on planar substrates may substantially overestimate photodesorption from the thin ice mantles of cosmic dust.

papers.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
papers.authors: Zhiwei Chen, Marie Cassing, Paramvir Singh, Luciano Rezzolla
papers.abstract: Extended emission (EE) lasting hundreds of seconds has been observed in a fraction of short gamma-ray bursts (sGRB) containing both nonthermal and thermal components, and representing a significant puzzle for models involving binary neutron stars (BNSs). Recent GRMHD simulations of BNS mergers found that the late-time fallback is approximately quasi-spherical and motivated an r-process powered thermal model for EE. However, the available radioactive-heating power may be insufficient to sustain the luminosity inferred by such a model. We therefore propose a fallback-fed secondary-jet scenario in which a fraction of the fallback material circularizes on the black-hole equatorial plane and powers the jet, while polar fallback impedes its propagation. Using a semi-analytic toy model, we follow the propagation of the jet-head through the fallback envelope and identify jet-dominated, cocoon-dominated, and choked scenarios. The boundaries of these regimes depend primarily on the circularization fraction $f_{\rm circ}$, on the jet half-opening angle $θ_j$, and on the polar refilling factor $ξ_{\rm pol}$, with the approximate scaling $\widetilde{L}\propto f_{\rm circ}/(ξ_{\rm pol}θ_j^2)$. By post-processing data from BNS-merger simulations we find that the fraction of bound fallback material that avoids prompt capture is $f_{\rm npc}\simeq0.52$, thus providing an upper bound on the circularizable fallback supply. Under suitable prescriptions for nonthermal jet emission and thermal emission from the jet head, the estimated isotropic-equivalent $0.3$--$10$ keV energies reproduce well both the observed EE distribution for the jet-dominated branch and its low-energy end for the cocoon-dominated branch. Overall, these results suggest that fallback-fed secondary jets represent a dynamically feasible and energetically consistent explanation of the EE in sGRBs.

papers.title: Chromospherically Active Stars in the MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey
papers.authors: Okwudili D. Egbo, David A. H. Buckley, Paul J. Groot, Orapeleng Mogawana, Anke van Dyk, Yusuke Tampo, Simon de Wet
papers.abstract: Stellar magnetic activity has long been established to occur in subsets of late-type main-sequence stars and manifests itself in the form of chromospheric and coronal activity. This activity is driven by magnetic fields generated by dynamo mechanisms associated with stellar rotation and convection, which channel and dissipate magnetic energy to the outer atmospheric layers. Optical spectroscopic follow-up was carried out for 99 radio-X-ray coronally active stars of G-, K-, and M-spectral types in the SARAO MeerKAT Galactic plane survey point sources. There are 46 stars that exhibited chromospheric activity. Specifically, 39 stars show Ca II H&K emission lines, whereas 18 show Ca II IRT, 11 show both H&K and IRT lines. Of the 39 stars displaying H&K emission, 37 show activity levels greater than the Solar minimum activity. Their X-ray to bolometric luminosity ratios are within the coronal thresholds of > -4.5. In addition, we explored optical photometry to investigate the rotation information and found that these stars show short rotation periods; in comparison with activity levels, the activity levels dampen as the rotation periods increase. We also analysed optical light curves for a subset of stars, and they show flaring behaviour at the same epoch as enhanced chromospheric activity, indicating the flares and chromospheric emission are manifestations of the same underlying magnetic activity process.

papers.title: New optimisations for exact, scalable 2D Gaussian process inference, with applications to astronomical time-series
papers.authors: Mark Fortune, Neale P. Gibson, Benjamin Pope
papers.abstract: Astronomical datasets often consist of a grid of datapoints in two or more dimensions, such as images, spectroscopic time-series, and imaging time-series. Gaussian processes (GPs) are a powerful tool for dealing with correlated noise in these data, arising from both astrophysical and instrumental systematics. Despite this, popular GP optimisations such as celerite are largely restricted to 1D datasets. Extensions to 2D data typically come with limited flexibility or poor scaling. As a motivating example, this limitation is significant for transiting exoplanet spectroscopy with JWST, as current analyses typically assume each spectroscopic light curve is statistically independent, despite many potential sources of wavelength-correlation, including detector readout noise and stellar granulation. This introduces a potential bias in atmospheric retrievals which is typically ignored. To solve this problem, we present new, exact GP optimisations implemented in the JAX-based package luas, which extend 1D GP optimisations to multidimensional data using Kronecker product algebra. These GP optimisations are highly flexible, permit efficient analysis of 2D datasets containing millions of datapoints, and in many cases have a cheaper cost than transit light curve modelling. These optimisations are key to pushing the limits of exoplanet spectroscopy to smaller targets around bright host stars, as we increasingly hit instrumental and astrophysical noise floors. We suggest further applications to the analysis of ground-based high resolution spectroscopic time-series, extreme precision radial velocities, and high-contrast imaging, drawing on the connection that certain 2D GP models represent a probabilistic generalisation of PCA. Applications may even extend to machine learning and geostatistics, as we present novel optimisations for the Linear Mixing Model and the Linear Model of Coregionalisation.

papers.title: Estimations for strong and weak hot Jupiter magnetism: A Python package with interpolators and scaling laws
papers.authors: Albert Elias-López, Aline Vidotto, Daniele Viganò, J. R. Fuentes, Simon Müller, Emily Sandford
papers.abstract: Hot Jupiters (HJs) are commonly thought to host the strongest dynamo-generated magnetic fields among exoplanets, exceeding Jupiter's by up to an order of magnitude, which can potentially induce observable star-planet interaction (SPI) and planetary radio emission. However, while several indirect, model-dependent estimates of HJ magnetic fields have been reported from SPIs and recent transmission spectroscopy diagnostics, no unambiguous direct (radio) detection has yet been achieved. We aim to provide a range of magnetic field estimates for HJs, considering the mechanisms responsible for inflation and the convective flux entering the magnetic field scaling law. Given that their dynamos operate in the fast-rotating regime (Rossby number <~ 0.1), we combine one-dimensional evolutionary interior models with magnetic field scaling laws under two limiting heating scenarios: deep and shallow energy depositions. The deep-heating scenario maximizes convective heat flux in the dynamo and predicts strong magnetic fields of up to ~100 G, whereas shallow heating, which is arguably more realistic for most proposed physical mechanisms, weakens convection and yields much weaker fields of O(1) G. The strong field scenario is compatible with SPI indirect detections, and the weak field scenario is in agreement with recent atmospheric constraints. We derive scaling law relations based on observables (planetary mass, radius, and/or incident stellar flux): Bstrong = 19 M_P^0.6 R_P^1.7 G; Bweak = 0.8 M_P^1.5 R_P^-1.2 G. These predictions provide a framework for interpreting future atmospheric wind measurements, SPI signatures, and radio observations, which may ultimately discriminate between competing interior-heating scenarios.

papers.title: Probing Dark Matter via the Migdal Effect in LUX-ZEPLIN Data
papers.authors: Yang Yu, Lei Feng
papers.abstract: Sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles deposit little energy in conventional direct-detection experiments and are therefore difficult to probe, but the Migdal effect provides an electronic signal from atomic ionization accompanying the recoil. Using the new results of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a 4.2 tonne-year exposure, we evaluate the sensitivity of the Migdal effect to the spin-independent DM--nucleon scattering cross section. For masses between $350~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $10~\mathrm{GeV}$, the projected 90\% upper limits range from $6.5\times10^{-37}$ to $9.6\times10^{-42}~\mathrm{cm^2}$. These limits are then used to constrain the minimal scalar- and vector-mediator DM models. For the light-mediator DM model, the constraint on the coupling reaches $α\simeq 10^{-12}$, which is stronger than or comparable to the constraints from kaon decays, stellar cooling, and SN1987A.

papers.title: SEDust: A DUSTY-Based SED-Fitting Pipeline for Dust and Mass-Loss from AGB and LPV Stars
papers.authors: Hamidreza Mahani, Narges Rostami, Atefeh Javadi, Hedieh Abdollahi, Jacco Th. van Loon, Francisca Kemper, Alvaro Sanchez-Monge
papers.abstract: We present SEDust, an automated pipeline for spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting and the estimation of stellar mass-loss and dust-production rates. We apply this pipeline to quantify the mass-loss and dust injection rates in the dwarf galaxy NGC~6822, focusing on long-period variables (LPVs) and pulsating asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars as major contributors to dust feedback into the interstellar medium. The total stellar mass-loss rate is found to be $(3.70 \pm 1.16) \times 10^{-3}\ M_{\odot} \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Two alternative methods (an LPV-based estimate and DESK) give totals that differ from this value by factors of $\sim$2.3 (lower) and $\sim$2.4 (higher), respectively, which we adopt as an estimate of the method-dependent systematic uncertainty. A positive correlation between stellar luminosity, intrinsic reddening caused by circumstellar dust self-extinction, and mass-loss rate is observed. The specific mass-return rate from AGB stars is $(7.40 \pm 2.30) \times 10^{-11}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, indicating that mass return from AGB stars alone is insufficient to sustain the current star formation rate of NGC~6822. This result implies the need for external gas accretion or additional mass-return mechanisms.
